data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues against the panel's superiority as a base-rate artifact but its own mechanism undercuts the argument: majority voting suppresses false positives only if individual errors are random, yet random errors would equally suppress false negatives, producing accuracy above base rate — a genuine gain by SRC_002's own logic, not mere compliance. More critically, the claim that a checklist with high sensitivity but low specificity induces uninformative individual judgments is self-defeating: high sensitivity means the checklist correctly identifies positives, so individual judgments that follow it are informative about positives by definition. The base-rate artifact requires low sensitivity (always guessing negative), contradicting the stated high-sensitivity premise.
